headline: Keep power coupled to consequence. Expand agency. Build the path to repair.
intro: Boundary First Labs is an independent public-interest research and engineering laboratory. Its social mission is to help people and institutions build consequential systems that remain answerable to the people and conditions they affect.
closing: World class is what you give the world: more capability, better distinctions, stronger repair paths, and institutions more worthy of the trust placed in them.

title: Social Mission
headline: Better systems should leave people with more agency, not more invisible burden.
coreProposition: The systems that govern people's possibilities should remain answerable to the people, conditions, relationships, and futures that bear their consequences.
humanTranslationOfPrimaryHeadline: If someone bears the consequence, the system needs a way to see them, hear them, explain itself to them, and reach repair.

proHuman: People are agents, not merely users, workers, patients, consumers, data points, claimants, demographic categories, or administrative roles.
proInstitution: Institutions are human tools for carrying purpose, memory, authority, obligation, maintenance, and care across time; BFL seeks to improve them rather than merely oppose them.
proProgress: Scientific and technical capability should expand, while the systems for consequence, responsibility, contestability, maintenance, and repair expand with it.
antiSavior: BFL should increase people's capacity to understand, decide, contest, act, and repair; it should not create dependency on BFL as a permanent interpreter.

label: People
promise: Help people understand, navigate, contest, and repair consequential systems that affect their lives.
publicLine: You should not need extraordinary power, money, fluency, health, persistence, or luck merely to get a consequential error acknowledged and corrected.

label: Practitioners & communities
promise: Give practitioners and communities usable methods for seeing hidden burdens, mapping responsibility, preserving local knowledge, and improving the systems they already inhabit.
publicLine: The people closest to a system often carry knowledge the formal representation has forgotten.

label: Institutions
promise: Help institutions represent their real obligations, affected parties, maintenance needs, authority boundaries, and repair paths before defects are displaced onto people.
publicLine: Institutional capacity should reduce the amount of institutional incapacity that people are forced to absorb.

label: Human agency & dignity
humanPromise: A person remains more than the category through which a system encounters them.
failurePattern: A local model becomes the operative identity of the person and constrains options the system cannot adequately represent.

label: Standing, reasons, contestability & recourse
humanPromise: If a system materially acts upon you, there should be a meaningful route to understand it, answer it, challenge it, and reach someone capable of changing the outcome.
failurePattern: classification -> consequence -> no standing -> no appeal -> defect persists
claimPosture: normative and analytical; legal enforceability is jurisdiction-specific

label: Accessibility & non-normative participation
humanPromise: People should not have to approximate a normative user in order to exercise meaningful agency.
failurePattern: The system assumes one body, cognition, schedule, language, interface, resource level, or failure mode and treats variation as exceptional burden.
claimPosture: institutional and UX doctrine; specialized accessibility compliance requires applicable standards and review

label: Care, education & capability transfer
humanPromise: Good service should leave people more capable where doing so is safe and appropriate.
failurePattern: Knowledge remains institutionally gated until crisis, or support creates dependency without adequate continuity, recourse, or transfer of capability.
boundaryFirstOperation: give observable markers and safe actions
claimPosture: domain-specific evidence and reviewer gates apply, especially in health contexts

label: Economic dignity, labor & household continuity
humanPromise: People and households should not become the invisible buffer that makes a supposedly efficient system appear closed.
failurePattern: Benefits are counted locally while labor, maintenance, risk, precarity, or downstream cost is exported outside the accounting boundary.
claimPosture: analytical and normative; economic and legal claims require source- and jurisdiction-specific support

label: Public trust & bounded authority
humanPromise: Power that shapes unavoidable or essential conditions should remain explainable, contestable, bounded, and repairable.
failurePattern: Authority expands while meaningful exit, evidence access, appeal, named responsibility, or repair capacity disappears.
claimPosture: institutional and comparative-law design; not a statement of settled law

label: Humanly answerable software & AI
humanPromise: Automation should increase usable capability without becoming the place where responsibility disappears.
failurePattern: automated action -> real consequence -> opaque delegation -> nobody with practical repair capacity
claimPosture: governance and engineering doctrine; not universal safety certification

label: Public knowledge & educational access
humanPromise: People should be able to acquire the distinctions and tools needed to participate intelligently in systems that affect them.
failurePattern: Knowledge is abundant but structurally inaccessible, provenance is lost, and people remain dependent on institutional interpreters.

label: Ecological & intergenerational continuity
humanPromise: Today's systems should not preserve local success by silently consuming the ecological, infrastructural, or agency baselines required by future people.
failurePattern: Present benefit closes inside a narrow ledger while maintenance, ecological damage, resource depletion, and future obligations are exported across time and scale.
boundaryFirstOperation: test whether growth preserves its roots
claimPosture: systems and public-interest doctrine; empirical environmental claims require domain evidence

label: Maintenance, repair & durable public capacity
humanPromise: People should not have to repeatedly absorb the same institutional defect because maintenance and repair were never funded or owned.
failurePattern: construction is rewarded; maintenance, adaptation, incident response, and retirement are treated as residual overhead.
boundaryFirstOperation: make incident and correction paths visible

impactRule: Every social mission must connect human promise -> structural defect -> Boundary First operation -> public artifact or intervention -> evidence/review gate.
antiTheaterTests: Does the mission change budgets, authority, interfaces, review burden, maintenance, or repair paths?
Can an affected person identify what practical difference the commitment creates?
Is there an owner and an evidence path?
Are legal, health, and scientific claim ceilings visible?
Can criticism change the institution rather than merely be collected?
Does the institution transfer capability instead of manufacturing dependency?

claimFirewalls.legal: Rights, standing, due process, public trust, and remedy language may express BFL normative or comparative institutional doctrine. Do not present proposed principles as settled law. Jurisdiction-specific legal claims require primary sources and qualified review.
claimFirewalls.health: Agency, bodily literacy, accessibility, and capability-transfer language must not become diagnosis or individualized treatment. Safety, escalation, evidence, and clinical-review gates apply.
claimFirewalls.economic: Claims about markets, households, labor, damages, financialization, or public policy require explicit scope, evidence, and distinction between analysis, critique, and proposal.
claimFirewalls.environmental: Ecological and intergenerational principles may motivate systems design; empirical environmental claims require appropriate scientific evidence and domain review.
claimFirewalls.general: Social mission is not evidence that a BFL method works. Practical claims must earn support through implementation, affected-party feedback, comparison, criticism, and measured outcomes.

title: How we bind our own work
lead: The doctrine governs the laboratory before it governs anyone else.
commitments: Represent affected parties and residual burdens.
Give consequential decisions meaningful contest and appeal.
Give repair an owner with capacity.
Version material changes and preserve rationale.
Build stewardship and retirement before uncontrolled scale.
governance.humaneTest: Would you put your family inside this system?

headline: Challenge something we published.
body: If you think a Boundary First Labs claim, policy, record, or representation is wrong, incomplete, unfair, misleading, or missing a consequential distinction, we want a durable route for that criticism to land.

publicPosition: The work is substantial. The durable multi-person institution around it is still being built.
notYetClaimed: independent multi-person governance at mature scale
nearTermInstitutionalGoal: Turn accumulated work into publicly useful, bounded, inspectable forms while building the criticism, maintenance, stewardship, and governance structures required to support them.
longTermInstitutionalGoal: Become a durable public-interest steward capable of surviving correction, disagreement, transfer, and succession.

stewardship.headline: Stewardship is an institutional obligation, not an ornamental claim.
principle: Stewardship, correction, migration, retirement, institutional memory, and succession belong to the original design.
Stewards the research, methods, public record, criticism, collaborations, and consequence-bearing applications.
Turn accumulated work into publicly useful, bounded, inspectable forms while building the criticism, maintenance, stewardship, and governance structures required to support them.
Become a durable public-interest steward capable of surviving correction, disagreement, transfer, and succession.
Build stewardship and retirement before uncontrolled scale.
